within an unfolded clip's waveform or MIDI display. Shift-click extends an
existing selection within or across tracks; Shift plus arrows extends or
shortens it. Arrow keys move the insert marker in time or between tracks. On
macOS, Option plus left/right moves it to locators or selected-track clip edges.
Selection anchoring, ties and collapsed-track hit regions beyond this prose are U.

copy identity semantics are U (REQ-033).

the selected time; X returns through previous Z zoom states. Follow scrolls with
song position, pauses on editing/horizontal scrolling or a beat-ruler click,
and resumes on stop/restart or clicking an Arrangement/clip scrub area. Exact
viewport dimensions, animation timing and scroll thresholds are U.

R2 (ARR-B004/B005/B016/B018/B022–026): the Arrangement Overview spans the complete Arrangement and outlines its displayed portion. Horizontal/vertical drags scroll/zoom; within-outline double-click returns to the whole Arrangement. The beat-time ruler has the same drag axes; double-click zooms to selection, or the whole Arrangement without selection. Time-ruler horizontal drag scrolls. Progressive zoom uses +/− or Ctrl (Win) / Cmd (Mac) wheel/trackpad; CtrlAlt (Win) / CmdOption (Mac) drag pans. Optimize Height/Width and H/W fit the track/layout display. Alt (Win) / Option (Mac) wheel in a main lane vertically zooms the selected track, or all tracks with content in a time selection. Selecting Arrangement clip time also zooms the Clip View editor to it. Follow is offered by Control Bar and Options. Pause/resumption claims require genuinely moving playhead and automatically scrolling Arrangement before an actual pause trigger; stop alone does not promise moving scrolling while stopped. Current Clip R2 REQ031/CV063–067 owns the within-clip Overview and editor Follow contexts, not the Arrangement axes or Arrangement pause triggers. No viewport, timing or public dispatch formula is added.
title: Navigation, zoom and follow state

title: Persistence and teardown
Arrangement scrub inputs
contract: D-manual (A6.1, A6.3; ARR-B006/B036–039): with Permanent Scrub Areas enabled, clicking the Arrangement scrub area starts playback from the chosen point. Held left button repeats the area according to global launch quantization; jumps between points are documented as quantized. With that setting off, Shift-click in the Arrangement scrub area or beat-time ruler still scrubs. Settings owns setting exposure; Clip View owns its separate clip scrub. Quantized boundaries, repeated duration, actual playback, sound, default initialization and dispatch outcomes remain U; no scheduler law is inferred.

title: Device drop-area track creation
contract: D-manual (A6.1; ARR-B015): dragging an available instrument or MIDI effect into the Mixer Drop Area below Arrangement tracks creates a MIDI track; an available audio effect creates an audio track. This is the bare-device entrypoint, separate from Mixing existing-clip/device-chain drag. Unsupported device admission, failure, transaction, default routing and actual device processing remain U.

title: Waveform display zoom
contract: D-manual (A6.1; ARR-B017): Waveform Vertical Zoom Level enlarges the waveform display without requiring a clip-gain adjustment; its display setting applies to all Arrangement audio tracks and new clips as recorded. This is a display role, not an audio gain equivalence, waveform amplitude formula, recording-capture result or pixel mapping.

title: Public transport and Arrangement Position inputs
contract: D-manual (A6.3; ARR-B028–035): Play and Stop request Arrangement playback start/stop; space toggles playback. The insert marker determines the ordinary start position; Shift-space continues from the last stopped position. Home (Win) / Function-left (Mac) returns the marker to the starting play position. Double Stop remains Session REQ003. Selecting an Arrangement Position bars/beats/sixteenths field permits vertical drag, typed number plus Enter or up/down arrows; adjusting the fields moves the insert marker. The publisher initial-marker wording is documentation context, not observed factory/reset behavior. Engine timing, parsing, sample/beat arithmetic, competing starts, range/rounding and universal key interception remain U.

title: Chase MIDI Notes option
contract: D-manual (A6.3; ARR-B040): Options Chase MIDI Notes can deactivate/reactivate the documented chase behavior when playback begins inside a note. The publisher describes chasing as default; initial, saved/custom and reset histories remain distinct and unverified. This names an option and intended context only. Note messages, scheduling, audible output, numeric timing, channel/voice and default initialization remain U under the existing Playback late-note obligation.

title: Unfold and resize Arrangement tracks
contract: D-manual (A6.9; ARR-B104): the button next to a track name or U unfolds selected tracks to access clip time. The split line changes unfolded height; Alt+/Alt− (Win) / Option+/Option− (Mac) are named alternatives. Alt (Win) / Option (Mac) pinch resizes on a supported trackpad/touchscreen. Holding that modifier while resizing one track resizes all; modifier-clicking the unfold button or AltU (Win) / OptionU (Mac) unfolds all. Capability, actual key dispatch, limits, geometry, persistence and unsupported input hardware remain U.

title: Arrangement mixer entrypoints and control surfaces
contract: D-manual (A6.1, A6.15; ARR-B013/B019/B160–164): the Arrangement mixer is offered by View Mixer, CtrlAltM (Win) / CmdOptionM (Mac), and the bottom-right mixer control. View Mixer Controls customizes mixer controls; View Arrangement Track Controls separately customizes individual track controls. The source states shared values/settings between those surfaces; Performance Impact, track delays and crossfader are named mixer-only examples. Mixing REQ001/MXW001 already owns actual access to the section/components and individual controls; Engine ER006/007 and Mixing MXW015 own their named displays. No all-control bijection, new mixer coefficient, track-delay/CPU law, key interception or layout persistence is inferred.
